title: Update: Repeating Event Icon📅??
body:
Latest update added a Repeating Events Icon to iCal (can’t be turned off). This makes zero sense. U already have no space to describe an event in iCal. U can fit 3 or 4 characters, but now w/ the ‘Repeat Icon’, u only fit 2 . So “📅Vet” is now“Repeat Icon 📅Ve”
Clearly, Apple thinks we’re too stupid to remember a Repeat Event, so they need to do it for us…but then, I do only have 100s of icons to do myself. 

New feature, yet it only took seconds to find the question “How to remove Repeat Event Icon in iCal” in the 🍎 Community pages, & 100s of users already had the same question!

title: Please Add Hijri Date Adjustment
body:
Please add an option to manually adjust the Hijri (Islamic) calendar by +1 / -1 / +2 / -2 days.

Many countries, including Bangladesh, Saudi Arabia, India, Pakistan, and others, may observe Hijri dates differently based on local moon sightings. The current fixed calculation often shows incorrect dates for our region.

Most Android phones already provide a simple Hijri date adjustment option. Apple Calendar should offer the same flexibility.

This small feature would make the Hijri calendar much more accurate and useful for millions of Muslim users around the world.

Thank you.

title: Do Apple's sw engineers ever USE their Apps?
body:
Lost three Stars:  Most recent iteration does away with "HIDE ALL" for all Calendars, so for using Apple Calendar to search for past present or future events it sadistically makes arthritic hands go thru a meaningless waste of time clicking off all other myriad categories in order to usefully search their sole category of interest for one event, then have to go back to arthritically click all Calendars back on. 

After decades of using this program, you acquire a database of so many entries that you need to sift thru, that you need to be able to do this in order to have a productive tool in your hands.

Meaning, I am no longer allowed to use Apple Calendar for Search.  Apple gave me the middle finger.

Intentionally?  I doubt it. But:  Why do away with a useful feature, let alone the raison d'etre for this program, without running it by a study group first?!

title: Almost Perfect for Any Apple User
body: Apple’s calendar app has one leg up over the competition, and that is the integration with its products and services. I can ask Siri for the next event on my calendar from any of my Apple devices, and I can get personalized suggestions for new events as well based on conversations in iMessages or Apple Mail. There is one problem with this app, though, and it is the reason I did not give it 5 stars. That issue is the Apple Reminders integration. If I set a daily reminder, then that reminder will take over my entire monthly view of the calendar and make it so that I am unable to see the events I actually want to see. There is an easy way to fix this, and it is to make an option to not show a specific list of reminders in the calendar app. For now, though, I have reminders turned off. If this issue can be fixed, I will easily give this app 5 out of 5 stars.

body: I have used and liked this app for years. I don’t know when it happened, but now it’s got a problem with recurring events. Now it still asks, but displays only one option and that’s to apply to future events. I’ve tried cancelling out or otherwise leaving without clicking the only option, but then my changes are not saved. Why ask if there’s only one answer? title: I ❤️ this calendar app & all of its features, BUT some  changes would be VERY HELPFUL! And THEN 5⭐️!
body:
I do love the Calendar app on my iPhone, but it would help me keep better track of my cancelled/rescheduled appointments without needing to delete them if there was a way to cross out the words of the cancelled/rescheduled appointments. Can the Powers That Be please implement some additional writing tools such as formatting: Bold, Italicized, Cross Out, Underlined, etc., and effects: Text Color, Pulsing Text, Shaking Text, etc.? It would be VERY much appreciated! Thank you! 

Also, there must be a bug because searching keywords for past appointments doesn’t work very well anymore. It makes searching for my most recent appointment with any one of my doctors who I may not see more than once a year very difficult, or nearly impossible unless I manually search each day going backward. Even trying to remember which months in the past that I may need to manually search for said appointments can be tricky, so manually searching each day is quite tedious and time consuming. I don’t know what happened to the ability to search by keyword, but the ability to do so became very sketchy a few updates ago (I don’t remember exactly which one, sorry). Please, your help with this would be VERY much appreciated! Thank you!

One more feature would be the proverbial icing on the calendar cake! If you can add a way to include a picture of the doctors I have appointments with to my appointments when I open them, that would help me, and MANY others who may forget what some of their doctors look like, and would therefore also help to reduce the anxiety that many feel when needing to go to doctor appointments. Thank you VERY much for your consideration of this request! VERY much appreciated!

title: Deleted all my events
body:
I save EVERYTHING— my information for dates, appointments, work stuff, and just personal things on my agenda —in my calendar app. The NIGHT before I had a bit of a packed day and really was relying what I had marked on the app to remember where I was supposed to be and when, it just deleted everything. Seemingly randomly. Seemingly on its own. Google told me to re-sync my icloud, but nothing was saved, allegedly. I had to scramble last minute to get all the information I needed and reorganize my day before it even started, and it was still a complete mess. It wouldn’t even let me make new events so I had to get a whole different app that has incredibly bad UI, comparatively. 

Most of that definitely falls on me, ultimately, but a calendar app should really not be deciding to wholly reset on its own like it seems to have done. I do not think it is at all possible I accidentally deleted it myself since I wouldn’t even know how to begin with wiping the whole app like this. Not even my subbed calendars are on there, nor the categorized color tags I made. Safe to say I’m not relying on this app again. I’m just going to a paper calendar like a boomer because ALL these apps seem to have these random janky problems lol.

title: Not user friendly
body:
So many minor adjustments could make this app great, but it's quite lacking.
- currently it won't let me add a second alert to meetings I've been invited to. Just a bug, but needs to be fixed.
- once I "ACCEPT" a meeting invitation, please remove the accept/maybe/decline option at the bottom. It makes it unclear at times whether I've responded or not.
- I should be allowed to set standard alerts that automatically apply to every event that ends up on my calendar, regardless of who puts it there or created the invitation.
- the ability to share certain events or portions of the calendar should be more fluid and easy to set up.
- the ability to treat events like a "checklist" and cross them off while allowing them to stay on the calendar could be helpful.
- forcing "cancelled" events to be deleted is not always a good thing. Having a record of a previously scheduled event can be helpful at times.
- attaching notes/itineraries/etc to calendar events should be much more intuitive and directly accessible.

title: Subscription?
body:
I NEVER write reviews but I’ve been using this app for years and I’m very disappointed to see what’s happening with it. First of all, this app used to be free. One day they decided to show advertisements, causing you to almost feel forced into paying for the subscription in order to keep everything stored in it. I recently paid for the monthly subscription, it went a few days without showing advertisements and now showing them again today. You open the app and have to wait for the advertisement to finish before it displays the calendar. When I’m in the middle of booking an appointment for something over the phone, this is a huge inconvenience. When I saw the advertisement I thought maybe there was a glitch with them processing the payment for the subscription, but when I click on the new “pro” button they show so you can pick a plan, it shows that i am in fact subscribed.
So I would love to know why I’m paying monthly for this if it’s gonna still show me obnoxious advertisements that I have to wait for before I can use the calendar? Really makes no sense to me

title: Anniversary Options
body:
This review is for the developer team in charge of this app’s features: 
The calendar is useful in its current form. What it lacks and what I suggest be implemented is an option to mark an event as an anniversary event where if we choose to have the event be a recurring event then we can have calendar keep track of the days, weeks, months or years since the date of entry. Currently this is only available an option for birthdays where a particular contact has their birthday on their contact card. So, for example, if I want to memorialize the day my son died I have to create a new, additional contact and make his “birthday” on the day of the event. This option or toggle to track a given duration seems like a fairly easy thing to implement and would be infinitely useful to track time between points for any event one sees necessary. Please consider this feature addition to an already useful calendar application. Thank you.

title: iOS Calendar Alert Time Not Syncing with Exchange!
body:
Iphone IOS: 18.3.1

MDaemon 24.5.2

Notes: User has enabled a default reminder for new events for 15 minutes on MDaemon and user has also created a default time on iphone. (Settings > Calendar > Default Alert Times > Events 15 Minutes)

User work flow: User creates an event on iphone calendar application as standard and in alert section Default 15 minutes is checked off and user does not change. User creates the event and on the MDaemon side this time is not reflected the reminder section is off. If the user removes the default timer from their ios device settings and manully inputs desired time. When the event is created it then reflectes on the MDaemon side and the event shows whatever time the user selected.

This seems to be an exchange issue with iOS calendar application.

title: The Perfect Calendar for Organizing My Life!
body:
Apple Calendar is an absolutely essential app for staying organized and on top of my schedule. The interface is clean, intuitive, and easy to navigate, making it simple to add events, set reminders, and view my day, week, or month at a glance. I love how it syncs seamlessly across all my Apple devices, so I never miss an appointment, whether I’m on my iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

The integration with other apps like Mail and Maps is incredibly helpful, automatically adding events and locations for me, so I don’t have to manually enter details. I also appreciate the ability to set multiple alerts, share events with others, and color-code different calendars, which helps me keep everything organized.

Apple Calendar truly makes managing my time a breeze, and I can’t imagine life without it. It’s the most reliable, user-friendly calendar app, and I highly recommend it!

title: Somehow, this is STILL the best calendar app out there
body:
Every so often, I get frustrated with Apple software and subscribe to alternatives. "This is too simple. I need more." is usually how these periods start.

Over the years, I've tried Fantastical, Notion Calendar and other apps that I've long forgotten.

No matter how hard I try to adjust my workflow around those alternatives, I always crawl back to the simplicity and efficiency the built-in Calendar app and wonder why I decided to leave it in the first place.

Calendar doesn't have integrations. It doesn't have calendar sets, built-in weather, natural language parsing for creating events, or even many customization options. However, as an actual calendar, it cannot be beat.

Want to add an event? Hold an open time on the calendar.

Want to adjust the length of an event? Hold the outer edges of the event and adjust up or down as needed.

It's simple, but effective. And it's one less subscription!

title: We NEED an Attachment Option!
body:
This calendar is the only calendar I use. I’ve tried going to others and maybe it’s because I’m just so used to this one, but I can never really commit to any others besides this one. Granted, I am an Apple person through and through (all my devices) so I really don’t need to use another calendar app, BUT! …..this app really, really, REALLY needs to add an attachment feature. Being able to attach videos, photos, PDFs, Notes, etc to a specific event would be the biggest help not only in terms of work related things, but in terms of family related things.

I also understand that there’s already a Reminders app, but if I could use the calendar app for everything from scheduling events and appointments to reminders and task lists, it would streamline my life so much (and I can’t imagine it wouldn’t be helpful to so many others). So add an attachment feature (for multiple different attachments), the ability to schedule and view reminders, add a task lists feature with the ability to check off what’s been completed, and this app would be 5 stars all the way!

title: Some serious oversights
body: Generally, this app is good for keeping track of events and schedules. However, there are a few missing or flawed features that seem obvious. - Firstly, you can’t set a custom travel time. You can only choose from 5 min, 15 min, 30 min, 1 hr, 1.5 hr, or 2 hr, or could have a time based on map info for your starting location. This is an obvious problem, as travel times have a lot more variation than that, and I’ve had problems with the “Starting Location” feature. Why not give us 45 min? Or 3 hr? Or literally just let us set the time ourselves??? - Secondly, there is no way to set an event that repeats on the same day of the week per month (eg. second Saturday of each month). Considering many events are scheduled like this, it seems like a huge oversight. - And lastly, the timing for alerts has a similar issue as travel times, where we can’t just set a time ourselves and instead have to choose from a very restrictive list of options. I don’t know how hard it could be to just let us set our own time?? The app works fine overall, but I’ve had to do some annoying workarounds to get me alerted and leaving on time, and have had to individually set monthly events. These just seem like obvious problems that shouldn’t have gone unfixed by now.

title: Time Zones are Totally Fouled Up
body: Every time the time changes or I get on a plane Calendar changes the times of my appointments. They are always sending me to the dentist an hour early or late because daylight savings has kicked in or out. If I enter 9:30 as the appointment time it should always show 9:30. Any time a computer changes the time I have entered it is making it wrong. Even if I am currently on the other side of the planet my appointment is still 9:30. Additionally, the start and stop times for an event should be able to be set to different time zones. For example when you are flying. (The whole point of flying is to go somewhere else.) I shouldn’t have to calculate my arrival time in my departure time zone to enter it and I certainly don’t want to see my arrival time in my departure time zone. You should be able to set time zones like CST or CDT rather than have to figure out what city is in the same time zone. If it’s going to insist on doing it for you it should be smart enough to know that a time in November is going to be standard time not daylight time. I am just really tired of Calendar sending me to the dentist an hour late or early.

title: Inefficient, poor technology
body:
As a discerning user with a demanding schedule, I find it incredulous that Apple's Calendar software, touted for its simplicity and efficiency, still lacks the fundamental capability to streamline event management across multiple calendars. 

It is utterly baffling that in this era of technological advancement, I am forced to waste valuable time creating duplicates of the same event for each calendar, rather than having the option to seamlessly integrate one event across multiple calendars. 

This antiquated limitation not only impedes productivity but also reflects poorly on Apple's commitment to providing user-friendly solutions. As someone who values efficiency and precision in every aspect of life, I implore Apple's esteemed team of software engineers to prioritize this glaring oversight and implement a solution that aligns with the expectations of modern users.

I urge Apple to heed the frustrations of its loyal clientele and rectify this deficiency promptly, thereby reaffirming its reputation as a pioneer in intuitive technology. Failure to address this issue expeditiously risks alienating the very demographic that has propelled Apple to the pinnacle of success.

title: You Can’t Search More Than One Year — Wake Up, Apple!
body:
I use calendar more than anything else as it’s my daily planner and journal.  Simple, straight-forward, and basic.

It has a few idiosyncrasies or underbaked limitations, such as not being able to arrange the order of your different calendars—which is maddening because if you want to give priority to a newly-created calendar for a different category of activity, there’s no way to send it up the totem pole—except to delete older calendars and that’s not a feasible solution.

However, the ELEPHANT IN THE ROOM with this app has long been that Apple has intentionally decided to prevent searchability of more than a year forward/backward, which is absurd given that palm devices have been able to perform this most basic function for over twenty years.

The only apparent incentive is to encourage reliant calendar users to purchase an Apple computer so that the search in calendar can be broadened beyond one year.  Apple: isn’t it enough that people purchase an iPhone to use as their planner that you should include features typical of a planner, or is your Mac business model so dependent on getting those nasty iPhone calendar users to purchase a computer for Mac’s success?

Besides, if someone truly wants to get around this intentional impasse, they don’t need a Mac, they can simply find an alternative calendar such as Weekcal, Calvetica, et al — that will allow them to perform their search beyond one year.

Wise up, Apple.

The one feature that would make this calendar perfect is if the user had the option to activate synchronization with the items from Reminders app (or just have a separate separate “inbox” within the calendar app) that we could just drag and drop them onto a calendar day. 
This would save time having to retype calendar entries. I actually deleted Reminders because it’s completely isolated from Calendar.
Yes, I know I can drag items from reminders to calendar, but it’s gimicky and who likes having to check 2 separate, isolated apps to stay organized?
Plenty of calendar services have already activated tasks-calendar sync feature, so it’s surprising that Apple hasn’t done this yet. Such a missed opportunity and waste of computing power.

Also, I need to get rid of the blank squares between months. Sometimes it is an entire blank row—just a waste of space. There are many other great visual indicators for the month change.

Apple/iPad calendar is ROCK SOLID in reliability—I’m always impressed at how fast and error-free it syncs all the services. This the most important and programmatically difficult part. So, it’s sad that there are sooo few options that make it more usable for robust professional planning.

title: "Apple Calendar: Chaos Amidst Cosmic Disarray"
body:
In the intricate web of life, where even the cosmic ballet of celestial bodies seems simpler than the perplexing intricacies of our daily existence, the Apple Calendar app emerges as a bastion of both promise and disappointment. As humanity grapples with the interminable waits at traffic lights, akin to the eons passing between galaxies, the shadow of COVID hangs ominously over our lives, disrupting plans with the ruthlessness of a cosmic collision. Amidst this chaos, akin to the pandemonium following an emergency door breach, one would hope for the Apple Calendar app to be a beacon of order.

Alas, it falters on the precipice of our expectations. Its attempts to corral the unruly events of our lives often feel as futile as attempting to harness the unpredictable forces of the universe. The traffic light waits may be long, but the wait for the Apple Calendar app to provide seamless organization feels even longer, a cosmic irony in the grand scheme of our digital interactions. In the face of the tumultuous events that characterize our times, one longs for a digital sanctuary, a haven of meticulous planning. Regrettably, the Apple Calendar app, amidst its sleek interface, fails to mitigate the chaos, leaving us yearning for a celestial order in the midst of our earthly disarray.

title: I like this app but it could be improved
body: I like this app. Its easy to use and set appointments in it. You can even set repeating Events to some degree. Like most bills are due monthly so you can set an event like say a payment reminder for your Netflix or Disney+ account and set it to repeat monthly. You can even set daily, weekly, every 2 weeks, or, monthly events. There’s even a custom that lets you do events that say repeat every 2, 3, 4, or however many days you want to set it to repeat, but what it doesn’t have is a way to set an event that happens like every 3rd Saturday of the month. Because each month has different number of days in it you can’t use the every so many days function because it throws it off. Like for example if an event is every 4th Thursday of the month but the previous month had 5 Thursdays it would throw off the count. So having a way to specify every 4th Sunday or Thursday or whatever day of the month would fix this problem cause as for now I have to create an event for each month manually and that is super time consuming! title: Doesn’t sync with Outlook calendars
body: Calendar works great if you don’t have to sync any non-Apple calendars. I am a devout Macbook user but I have to use Outlook for work, and I like to have the calendar synced with my personal Apple calendars so I can see my availability according to personal appointments and school events that I’d rather not put in my work calendar. I had no problem setting up the sync, but it often drops it or randomly doesn’t sync certain appointments, with no rhyme or reason. Sometimes it will sync the same appointment three times. When an Outlook meeting has been canceled, it is not removed. I have always used Calendar without any issues or complaints, but I am now going to subscribe to a third-party application, to avoid missing important work meetings, or double booking and having to cancel something. It’s really disappointing, because searching online for a solution, I could see that lots of other people are having this issue, and there seems to be no interest in solving it. The only solution offered by Apple support was to delete the calendar, and set it up again, which is the equivalent to “ turning it off, and turning it on again.”  Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn’t, and even when it does work, the problem returns the following day or week or just when you start to get comfortable, it doesn’t sync your appointments and you miss an important meeting.

title: Only missing 1 thing
body:
The ability to add the same event to multiple calendars in one event.  I share calendars with different people and the ability to select and event and add it to more than one calendar at a time would be amazing.  Okay wait 1 more.  

The ability to undo all the birthday’s that were added to the calendar by Facebook a few years ago.  I can not seem to undo that action accept for manually.  

Okay, last feature upgrade request I swear.  Keep in mind, I am a power user.  The ability to scroll through things that are in all day without going to a different view.  

With all of that said, I could not live without this calendar. I use it all day everyday. I manage around 15 calendars feeds and shared calendars in this one app and i could not live or work without it.

body:
Spectrum oversells it’s Internet services! It is even WORSE beginning on Friday nights through Sundays.  The Internet  service begins to decline at around 5 PM and steadily worsens as the evening progresses.       Although I pay AT&T for mobile ice when I don't have access to the Internet, the quality is pathetic. 

Please note that Apple is my FAVORITE company. What is happening is not Apple‘s fault. It is imperative that they become aware of what is happening with the companies that sell Internet services as their devices are highly dependent on Internet service. Several times on Saturday and Sunday nights, I can’t even get my iPad third generation to even turn on! I urge Apple to become involved in the movement to stop the fraud FRAUD perpetrated by companies that offer Internet service. It is 100% unacceptable that they get away with and inability to provide quality Internet Service 24 hours per day.           

In the past, all my Apple devices would  sync including the CALENDAR.I know so many people that have the same problem. Unfortunately, they blame Apple!

The only problem I have with Apple is that in the past when I would dictate or type a sentence and put a period at the end of the sentence. It would automatically know to capitalize the first letter in the next sentence. once in a while it will not. (Notice I didn’t correct the last sentence). title: Great, but wish there was a way to remove extra days in-between months
body:
ICal is great- quick and easy to use! I like the use of different colors; I like the ease of use. Would love to have the option to remove national holidays, or religious holidays, but that’s an issue with every calendar. 

One thing continues to bug me, though: I wish that it was possible to view the transition between months seamlessly. Currently, there are always extra days on the calendar in-between months. Sometimes it’s an extra 4, 5, or even six days! 

This might seem insignificant to software developers, but I teach five classes a semester. Often, I organize assignments for major projects by counting the number of weeks after I introduce the instructions: two weeks to choose a topic; two weeks further to get an outline going; four weeks to complete the annotated bibliography, etc. 

I do this for five classes, paying attention to what will come in grading-wise for each course. It’s a tricky thing to plan multiple weeks across multiple classes, and strike a balance. 

The issue with the false extra days drives me batty, and makes this task exponentially harder. Please at least provide the ability to adjust this in iCal. 

Thanks!

title: Appointment Keeping & Scheduling Tasks
body:
I highly recommend Calendar. It has numerous features that allow one to organize their day and even coordinate specific events with others. 

This app has really helped me to keep appointments when I am in the midst of doing other things. With the Alert feature, I can receive reminders to help me wind down whatever I’m doing and be ready to leave at the appointed time. With the Travel Time feature, I can set the time I need to leave for an appointment by choosing a location to leave from, in which case it figures the time to reach the destination automatically; or choose my own timeframe for travel. Either of these block off the additional time needed for travel on the daily schedule. 

Calendar has also greatly helped me to get organized — to schedule out tasks that require handling. Before using Calendar, my tasks continued to be postponed and remained undone and disoriented in timeline and priority in the Reminders app. Having the tasks on my calendar helps me see the full day at a glance; what I need to do on a certain day; and block off sufficient time to complete each task. If I don’t get a task completed on the assigned date, I can either edit it to move the task to another day, if I didn’t work on it at all; or edit it to be a repeating event to work on until I complete the entire task.

title: Handy but not quite polished
body:
It is very nice to have my calendar in my phone so it is always with me. And it is great to be able to see my wife's calendar and she mine.

But this app has a big problem.

I missed several important appointments by showing up at the wrong time before I caught this Calendar app in the act of changing event times and realized that it was the problem.

When I am making an appointment, the natural flow for me is: I create a new event in the agreed date, then I enter the agreed time, then I enter the name and place.

Calendar does not cooperate with that flow. When I enter the name, it silently goes and changes the time to match that of the previous event of that name. It goes and silently changes that which I explicitly entered just a moment earlier! That is unacceptable.

If I were entering the name FIRST in a new event, then I can see how automatically setting the time could be helpful. But when I have already set the time, changing it silently is outrageous behavior.

Here is my suggestion to the developers. Before the app goes and automatically fills in any field, it should pop up a window asking permission to do so. And every field should allow a value representing blank or unset, and this should be its default value when a new event is created.

title: needs alerts AHEAD of appointment ⏰
body:
I would have given this app five stars, except for the fact that it does not allow you an option to send you an alert in advance of the event. for example, if I have an appointment on May 20, the option should be given to alert you a few days ahead of your appointment.
This app does allow you to repeat the app AFTER the scheduled date and time, but it certainly would be more helpful to be reminded that you have an event coming up without having to go in and actually look at the calendar. If there is a way to do this, I wish someone would let me know. the way I do it now is schedule my appointment three days in advance on the calendar and have it repeat for three days.
Other than that it is a solid4-5 star application in my opinion.

title: Intuitive for many actions
body:
I don’t use the calendar for much more than an average person needs. It is absolutely perfect for my needs. I love that I can create events in certain calendars and show only whatever I need but turn on other calendar events when I want them. For example, I can make a calendar of my doctor appointments and a different one for friends’ birthdays. When I really need to know my doctor appointments, I may not care about Birthdays, nor the NASA and space craft events calendar that I downloaded. 
 
In the adding of events and use of the calendar, the editing and adding for the event is fairly intuitive. It is not difficult to find the correct buttons for editing or replacing. There is a little bit of needing to simply go into categories to find out how they work, but there are not enough of to them to take up large amounts of time in searching.
I like using this calendar very much. Especially when it pulls information from an email or another communication app. 

All the other apps that have looked appealing sale in one of the ways calendar has spoiled me. I haven’t needed another calendar app.

title: My rating is based strictly on the widget options.
body:
The month widget is so outdated, small, & lacks features like holidays & weekly forecasts at a glance like Samsung’s Calendar widget for Galaxy devices.

I miss having a monthly view widget on my Home Screen showcasing holidays, events, weekly forecast, & etc on the widget itself “without having to touch or open the widget”.

The Calendar widget on Samsung Galaxy devices, is very similar to a physical calendar that you’d hang up but it includes weather icons beside each date for the next 7 days, & each month always includes the last few days of the previous month & the first few days of the upcoming month.

Your monthly view widget needs to at least increase in size to a standard large widget horizontally, which will give you room to add all holidays underneath each date & weather icons.

title: “Traveling” dates
body: For some reason, when I am adding appointments to my calendar, the date changes before I can save it. For example. I have a doctor appointment set for monday may 15, so while I am making the appointment, I am adding it to my iCal same time I am making the appointment. Then sunday may 14 comes, and up pops the appointment reminder from ical. Well, obviously a physician is not in office on sunday, so what is going on is what I am thinking. Now, on monday morning I call the doctor’s office to inquire when my ACTUAL appointment is, to find out it is in fact on mon may 15!  This is exactly what has happened to me in the past, much to my dismay!  So now, EVERY SINGLE TIME I attempt to make any type of appointment, I must confirm and reconfirm the correct date, because literally every appointment I attempt to schedule starts out with me opening the correct date and by the time I hit save has changed to the day prior to the actual scheduled appointment!!  This is both frustrating and time consuming as I have to continually confirm and reconfirm the correct date!  Thus, my review title of “traveling “ dates, which is not to represent that I am getting on a plane or having a road trip, but the fact that the date of my actual appointment changes before I hit the save key. Apple truly needs to fix this. This is a problem among many, which was not always happening with my phone, it just started one day!  As I tell my husband almost daily when a new problem appears with my phone that was never a thing before.…”steve jobs is absolutely ROLLING IN HIS GRAVE over all of the new, simple to fix, problems that appear on a regular basis in all of my family’s phones!!!!”  FIX IT APPLE!!!!  There are SO MANY MORE complaints I have about my phone which is becoming more and more of an expensive paper weight by the day!!!!!!!!

title: Do the developers use this app?
body:
I still miss the calendar on my Palm Pilot.  For two reasons:

1) if had an appointment on the Palm Pilot at 6:00 AM and another at 10:00 PM both would show up on one page. It was easy to scan from page to page and see future appointments. With the Apple Calendar it is necessary to turn the page and then go to the bottom of the page. 

2) I HATE the way events update. If I schedule a lunch for 1:00 in New York. It immediately shows as 11:00 AM here in San Diego. If I am traveling between here and NY and want to check my schedule I must figure out what time zone I am in and do the math. 

I am sure someone in the world likes those two features but I am yet to meet that person.

title: Drawbacks/ severe weaknesses in the Calendar.
body:
1) every time I open it it opens under one specific category,for instance “travel”.
2) after only
A few personal choices of categories I don’t have any option to add more, I like to categorize my entries to more easily search for items. For instance I’d like to have a new category of “doctors” but I no longer have any option to do so. And it doesn’t seem I’m able to delete, change, modify previous choices ??
4) often it seems  that after an IOS update it seems that previous entries like Doctor appointment info have disappeared into the abyss ???
Many people I come in contact with have said the very same thing and these are intelligent tech savvy people, I was an electronics tech Ian for 46 years, so it’s not that I’m not capable of figuring things out. 
It’s so frustrating to have appointments and even contacts just disappear from my calendar because I depend on that data when I’m inputting times, dates, descriptions of my health to share with the next doctor and find that there isn’t any records at all of my previous visits. I’ve been searching locally for an old school daily planner to fall back too to record important data because calendar is less than helpful to me these days and even those are hard to find now !
So I bought a big desk blotter calendar to write things down on. Does that give you enough input as to how much Calendar is failing us all, and it’s not just me. People I know are all buying calendars , ordering Day Planners and no longer depending on Calendar because in many ways it’s become less than useful, actually a liability because we loose the data we took the time to input and it affects our health decisions !?!?!

title: SO PRACTICAL
body:
I have made more use of the Calendar since I retired than when I was working: personal, car repair, doctor and many other appointments; anniversaries & birthdays; social events; getaways; and the occasional job like election judge. So not only does it help me keep track of my life events but through the family sharing option it also helps my wife and I coordinate appointments that involve both of us.

Another feature that I enjoy is how the app pulls up information from a similar past event as you create a new appointment. For instance when I create an Eye Dr appointment, the app will present the info that I can select from my last appointment if I named it Eye Dr; I may have to adjust the time and date but it certainly convenient to have some of the details entered automatically.

Life at work was so uncomplicated!

title: Cmon Apple… A Calendar; Stuck In Time
body:
With all of Apples accomplishments & their beautiful streamlined language translating with superb ease, I have full confidence the content will share from (my) device to device without much effort from the user, and therefore it serves it purpose…. But it could be better and needs to be much better to align with the competition of independent app developers. Hey Apple, instead of creating new emojis or Siri Voices for the always anticipated rollout of the updated iOS.. Why not talk about when the Calendar is going to get its big shining moment? 

The interface is boring. The environment overall too monotone even with the added agendas and  user modified options, to actually build any type of excitement for the day, yet alone for the days ahead of our all busy schedules. 

To be able to prioritize items in an a manner of which you can choose it to have a slightly larger font or theme would be nice. To have a helpful AI be an option to enable helping those of us who need that extra push, by using medically proven techniques to help those with ADHD organize our schedule better. Or auto default a completely oddball notification tone for those of us who become irritated or tone deaf to the customizable notification tones by doing it FOR us… again using a sort of medically researched method that doesn’t require the user to choose these individual tones but rather to be alarmed by them by default when it is best thought that the particular person with whatever condition or lack thereof would benefit from….as an across the board type of response to grab the attention without silencing the sound automatically, thereby losing its intended purpose. 

Why not give us the option to allow the IOS to read our random screenshots or pics we took …to look for dates/times of events we want to later remember but then don’t bc those shots got gobbled up by our endless photo album somewhere over the rainbow, safely tucked away in the iCloud, until we later discover by accident and way past the event we thought would have been cool to attend.

Just food for thought with an Apple a Day-
Thx Audrea

title: Functional
body:
I'm coming from a background of not really using calendars other than to see what day of the week a particular day might land on, or when a holiday is or something. I'm starting to use calendars more and more - and Apple's built in calendar app especially.

The different views are kinda neat, but not always particularly rich or interesting. Sometimes I wish there was a view more catered to specific things like tracking habits or something. I imagine views that would be more helpful. The typical views are all we get basically for now. But hopefully they will start adding some more interesting ones.

Still, with it just how it is, I am finding it easier and easier to plot out some plans. Adding doctors appointments or putting a concert on the calendar is helpful. Definitely like adding the locations to my appointments so it reminds me when I need to leave. Alerts are great to have - more than one especially. On iPhone and iPad well... all we get is 2 max. On Mac I can add multiples. The other alerts show up on iPhone and iPad if I put them in on Mac. I just think they ought to enable that capability on mobile devices.

One tip I can recommend if you want to add locations, is go to Apple Maps and drop a pin just before you add your appointment (or after if you haven't yet added a location). When you do, the location just gets offered up straight off, so you don't have to search for it in Calendar (since it is quirkier than in Maps).

Also, some creative uses for Calendar you may not have considered:

1) Journaling (make a Journal calendar & add appt entries when you're writing - write your journal in the notes of the appt)
2) Mood & Gratitude (make calendars for mood and gratitude journaling... you could use ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ for a great day in your event title)
3) Emoji use in event titles and calendar names

I keep a standard calendar, a work calendar, a health calendar, a journal calendar, and several others... but those are the ones I utilize most.

Birthdays come up automatically when people's birthdays are in their contact info, so I utilize that instead of manually adding it to the calendar. If you get way too many, you can go and edit their contact info and just copy their birthdates to the notes and delete the birthday field. I've disabled syncing with Facebook because it gives me wayyyyyy too many bdays and I just want to see the ones that are important to me.

And another tip is to use alarms in conjunction with Calendar. If I have something really important and I can't be late.. I'll sometimes set an alarm for "get ready to leave" and one for "leave now". I obtain these times by going to Google Maps and checking directions, swiping to the bottom to get reminded to leave on time, then set "arrive by" to when I want to get there minus about 15 minutes or so ... the estimated time to leave it generates will almost never get you in trouble even in pretty bad traffic. The down side is you could be a bit early, but better early for something important than to be chancing being late. You can do the same thing with Apple Maps, but it underestimates in my experience and I might be late if I calculate with that. Comparing the leave-by times between Apple and Google you'll see it's a stark difference. Lastly, don't think to use Reminders for this "reminder" to leave... Reminders' notifications aren't nearly as robust and can often be missed. So I don't use it for anything time sensitive. An alarm won't stop ringing until you specifically stop it or snooze it. If you don't need snooze you can disable that in your alarm setup for each specific alarm. I have many.

title: Calendar app is great, but…
body:
Best thing with calendar app is scheduling things, then being reminded, inviting people, etc.
However, when it comes to inviting people, it’s not that great…
I’m not sure what pops up for people when I invite them, but all I see is “invite sent” and sometimes the people say they didn’t get one at all. 
Then I end up sending the invite for calendar event to 2 of their emails AND their phone number. 
So now I’m basically sending 3 invites to one person to get it to work.

Ontop of this, I have a name I like my friends to call me, and a name my mother calls me.
When I invite people, I can’t choose literally anything about the invite.

I can’t choose when it’ll be sent to them, I can’t choose what name I want to be for specific invites, etc.
You should be able to customize invites so that you can make yourself something like

“Owner of 192 oak tree road”

Invited you to “House renovation - Thursday”
Date “Thursday ##/##”
Reminder One day before
Second reminder

And if you wanna send a calendar invite to your mother?

“Tyrone”
Invited you to “robin’s birthday party!”

The point is that you should be able to customize what your name is for invites on calendar.
Invites on calendar app need a serious update haul, and needs to be seriously streamlined.

The invites portion of it is the most important part and yet it’s complete garbage.

Also, when I wanna invite someone, it should be as simple as selecting a contact on your phone, and they get a pop up on sliding up your screen on iphone that they have to accept or decline or swipe down on a to deal with later.

title: Older you get, gets more helpful
body:
I schedule everything on it…..daily, weekly, monthly and long term.  I find it especially helpful with monthly and long term events/tasks like…. Cleaning  air filters once a month, checking oil tank level, emptying house vac, testing fire alarms, and the list goes on and on with tasks that need to be done but that you just don’t think about.  OR when you do think about it, you can’t do it because you are rushing out or can’t remember when you last did it. Of course annual reminders for birthdays, anniversaries, etc. are obviously important but so are reminders to have your furnace cleaned, winterize your irrigation system, etc.  All the things that need to be done but often you don’t think about it until it’s an issue.   It also helps to let you know when you last did a task assuming you followed through on it.  Trust me…. The busier you get the more it helps and the older you get, the more it helps!

One of the best features for me is the two alerts that are allowed with each entry! A week, 2days, 2hours, they are  all useful depending on the event/task.

title: Beware – Notifications Deleted!
body:
This app used to allow multiple notifications, (1 hour, 1 day, 2 days, 3 days, +) which I had set for several repeating events, then without warning Apple decided to limit all events to no more that 2 notifications, and reset all those to a default of 2 days. Not realizing I wasn't getting the notifications I'd set, I missed important deadlines and due dates and lost $$ because of it. The really messed up part is you can still set multiple notifications on the desktop version of the app, but even if you have your computer and iPhone calendars iCloud synced, YOU WON'T ACTUALLY GET THE NOTIFICATIONS YOU SET. This app is useless to me now. 
BRING BACK MULTIPLE NOTIFICATIONS, APPLE.

title: A Useful System App from Apple
body:
I have used Calendar for awhile and has helped a lot for organizing over the years so I figured I would share my thoughts after it popped up in the app asking for a review today. 

Calendar has always been useful for my family and I to keep track of everything in our lives. We can easily share appointments, birthdays, and other events in one place.

We can also create different calendars for ourselves and for everyone in our family. This makes it easy for everyone to stay updated on events and to share information with each other.

It's important to note that these features are not unique to this app. However, this app works well and is fully integrated across all of our Apple devices. This is a plus compared to other third-party apps. All in all, a winner in the calendar app category for me.

title: ICalendar
body: I love iCalendar more than any other resource. It keeps my husband & I on the same page as we share our calendars, thanks to Apple Technical Support’s assistance when setting up our shared calendars. It makes recurring events a cinch - just add the information and when you want it to recur and for how long. You can then modify any or all of the recurrences. All subsequent appointments are easy to add because the locations autofill. I just click on the address on the day of my appointments if I need directions. It will even alert me to the time I need to leave if I set it up to do so. I even put recurring chores on my ICal, such as for changing my air handler filter and my electric toothbrush head  every 90 days, weekly chores, etc., etc., etc. There’s no end to it’s usefulness and convenience.

title: Almost useless since ios7
body: Since the redesign in ios7 this calendar app is mostly useless.  The flat design makes using it a chore.  First it opens to a day planner view, which, unless you are using it to schedule your entire day, it is unnecessary.  Also that view’s design is barely understandable.  It’s hard to see where one day ends and another begins.  For most people, when they want a calendar, they want to open it and see a calendar, not a day planner. Getting to the calendar (month) view is infuriating.  There is no clear way to get to it.  Apparently you have to click on a word.  Makes no sense.  Once in the actual calendar view, there is little utility to it unless you only need to track one category of appointments.  If you want to look at the month and see where your doctor appt is compared to a work appt or a kids school play, you have no way of telling as the calendar only marks one grey dot to tell you there is something scheduled for that day.  If you actually use the calendar to schedule a lot of stuff, it is just a sea of grey dots with no way to tell them apart.  Finally, the actual design of the every calendar I’ve used since I learned to write, used a grid to make it easier to see what day of the week you are looking at.  This one bafflingly uses just horizontal lines.  Which makes looking at a glance to see what you have for the month an exercise in frustration.  Apple, FIX THIS APP!!!!

title: It’s the little things …
body:
Just a little bit of background first :
A 20 yr BA & PM in Information Technology, then construction & engineering, I was back-and-forth between android & PCs, and Apple products. 4 yrs ago I finally made a full conversion to Apple. Not only for love of the brand, but also the “accessibility” features. I now live with - to care for - my disabled, elderly dad who is also mostly illiterate. The potential in the future of “AI” aside, absolutely nothing compares to the accessibility features offered w/the iPhone. 

Not only is my (unbelievably) hectic personal life at task, but also mobilizing structure and facilitating order with my dads entire life,  assisting an older brother in collaboration with the VA and Community Support services for civilian Doctors & resources to combat cancer, and coordinating with my grown children to assist with school, sports and other activities.

My opinion is that the need me exists to (overhaul ?) the calendar, tasks, & reminders.

title: Stable and reliable, but needs more dynamic viewing options
body:

However, if you would like to look at your day, while also knowing what is coming up in your week/month or move appointments across dates, it is somewhat limited and makes you switch views.  For example, if i want to reschedule a meeting that is today till next Tuesday, I would like to know what is on my cal on Tuesday and what my openings are around that day while rescheduling.  If I had a small week forward preview in my day view that would help, and month forward in my week view etc. Drag and drop of meeting across weeks/months could work better too in effectuating this.  

Further, as a way of being a great time management tool it also would be nice if the app integrated with the Task app/list better, as most tasks are just unscheduled calendar items anyway.  The two should work and viewable together.

title: Easy and uncomplicated
body:
There are several benefits to using the calendar app on an iPhone:

1. Organization: The calendar app can help you keep track of your schedule, appointments, and events, and ensure that you don't miss anything important.

2. Reminders: The app allows you to set reminders for upcoming events or tasks, which can help you stay on top of your schedule and be more productive.

3. Syncing: The calendar app can sync with other apps, such as your email client, to ensure that you have all of your events in one place.

4. Sharing: You can share your calendar with friends, family, or colleagues, making it easier to coordinate schedules and plan events together.

5. Travel: The app can help you manage your travel plans by allowing you to add flight details, hotel reservations, and other travel-related information to your calendar.

6. Accessibility: The calendar app is easily accessible from your iPhone's home screen, making it easy to quickly check your schedule or add a new event.

Overall, the calendar app on the iPhone is a useful tool for managing your schedule and staying organized.

title: Okay - but not as customizable/user friendly as I would like.
body:
I have been using the calendar app for quite awhile, and it’s possible I just don’t know how to use it correctly, but I am honestly kind of annoyed by it. It doesn’t (as far as I know) allow for customization of the appearance etc of appointments in the calendar (changing their colors - some are blue and some are red, but I have no idea how to make things I put in there a specific color). I know that one time it read my emails and took a random meal cooking schedule and imported it, but it has never done that before or since then. Having the ability to easily, in app, in appointment, set the color and every parameter of the scheduled item would be so much better. The monochrome of the entries as is doesn’t help me at all. 

It also leaves a lot to be desired with regards to notifications - I get dozens of notifications a day from bunches of different apps, and the little notifications from the calendar just get lost in the noise more often than not. It would be ideal if the calendar would allow for scheduling optional alarms in the alarm app (cross talking between the two apps) that will go off at specific user set times instead of just having another little “ding,” and allow for as many of those alarms as desired instead of just one or two. At present I have no idea how to do that if such a thing is possible at all. Currently I just set alarms to go off prior to my appointments on the day/week of if I can remember to do that. It shouldn’t be that difficult though. I can’t tell you how many meetings I have missed because I didn’t remember it and my calendar app didn’t remind me in a way that would break through the noise of my day.

Beyond these two things, I reckon there are other things that I would like changed, but none so much as these.

title: Mid-choosing dates!
body: Generally good, but Calendar needs a “pause” to confirm date. Too frequently, I enter an event thinking I have chosen the correct day and date. But alas, I click the “Add” button, only to have my entry disappear! Although Calendar allows me to scroll to the date I want, it changes the date to some other date. Then I have to go search for it—never fun! For those humans who need a wee more guidance than the nerds, please give us a pop-up allowing us to “confirm” the date either at the “Add” button, or at sometime before [perhaps the date should be our first entry]. Of course, pop-ups have become irritating too, so you may want to have faded pop-ups suggest confirmation instead. Thanks.

title: Ok less issues
body:
Calendar is on for basic use of recording a few appointments, tho It works much better in a desktop than a phone. But if you have a busy schedule, rely on your calendar to keep you on track, and/or need to share appointments etc., then it isn’t for you bc it works poorly with all of that.
Making changes to the calendar is a crap shoot bc sometimes it works and sometimes the calendar deletes newly added appointments in front of your eyes, or after saving an events details and seeing it appear in the calendar, for whatever reason the calendar randomly forgets minutes later and changes it to a blank new event. If you just sit and watch it, the calendar will change before you eyes like this. Therefore it is NOT reliable.
Changes made on the phone don’t always pull to the app on the desktop and vice versa. So changes may or may not update for other devices, and you will likely have to do most everything in the calendar multiple times bc of the issue risking errors and confusion, which is totally unreliable and unacceptable for a calendar app.
Also shared items will create an issue of endless and useless busy work and restrictions. If you make a change to a shared event/appt, the other member(s) of the calendar get a notice for each minuscule change even if the item was changed back and deleted…so a typo could result in dozens of notifications that all have to be cleared individually by both involved parties. It is a frustrating and ridiculous waste of time. Yet if a party that didn’t create the entry needs to add details or make changes, they cannot…the only thing the calendar does is send a untimely and unuseful email saying this person wants to propose a change but it doesn’t link back to the event and you can’t accept changes, it’s just another useless notice sent that doesn’t help in any way…the “organizer” has to hunt for the item and make the changes manually and then the other parties get another useless notice to clear, so again, every event results in many notifications even if you’ve not set the app for notifications.
I have lost so much time and a ton of work specifically bc of the issues with the calendar, not to mention flat out missed spots bc they didn’t pull to all devices. I have so much in it that I haven’t gone another app route but also bc of costs. title: Wish there was more flexibility with Alerts
body:
I like that the calendar remembers events and addresses to make it easier to schedule. But when I want to have an alert for an event it is at 0900 the day, the day before and 2 days before.  I would like to set how often and when I am alerted to an event, 0900 is only important to business people. People outside the business world may be busy at 0900 and miss the alert. 
Also,I would like to send events to sms text so people can add them to their android calendar. My husband has Samsung and Google. I have Apple and IOS. It is so true you like one or the other. I am a victim of identity theft and it happened while I had Google and a Samsung phone. I will never go back. He however doesn’t like that Apple controls everything. So I need a way to send him the kids events and my appointments so that they go directly onto his calendar. I do all of the scheduling for the family and it would be nice if his calendar was updated and he didn’t have to keep asking me what appointments there were for the week. 
I would also like to see a little more privacy with the calendar. My daughter and I both have Apple. I share the purchases and Apple One with her. There are appointments I like to keep to myself. Like my psychologist or gynecologist. I am sure she wants the same privacy. With my passwords changing daily on my Apple phone and Apps and my phone and watch settings constantly changing I just want to know there is some privacy. Yet still there is more privacy on Apple then Android. One day hopefully hopefully the government will crack down on cybersecurity until then nothing is safe online.

title: Vanished
body:
Calendar app simply vanished from my iPhone screen.  Yesterday it was there, this morning it is not.  There is no visible screen or dock icon.  Furthermore, the AppStore doesn’t doesn’t offer a reload option.

The following parade of solutions have not worked: Shut down/restart, “pushed” calendar event from MacBook Pro, searched for app, and when “found,” the search sends me to settings.  Calendar WILL open when one clicks on a specific event, however, the app icon does not reappear.

Last resort: Synch to my laptop.  Possible issue: My MacBook Pro desktop icons randomly disappear.

Last idea as to why this is happening could be the large amount of data being stored on both devices. But that SHOULDN’T be an issue as information checks reveal plenty of space on both devices.  (And yes, all diagnostics have been run on both devices.)

The point has been made on countless boards for as long as they’ve existed: Apple must run itself.  One is left to wonder if, as discussed in Timothy Lanzone’s award winning film, Traveling Salesman (2012), P versus NP has been solved.  Apple’s computers are capable of answering their own questions without considering an answer’s real-time ramifications; but I digress. (Note: Theoretical computer scientists-please do not lash out at me from the darkness of my closet.  I am merely an enthusiast who has gained access to Prometheus, and has no clue as to how to “shut it down.”

Like many of you, I am weary of complaining about Apple.  We, the crew of OS Flying Dutchman are doomed to sail the Sea of Zeros and Ones on winds whipped by The God of The User-Friendly Graphical User Interface who demands sacrifice from his unsuspecting acolytes: unsuspecting public beta testers.

title: It would be better if….
body: All the separate calendars have a color to identify it. That entry could be from Apple (President’s Day) or from one or more of the users calendars - there’s no way to tell by glancing at that full month page if there’s something that needs to be looked at or if it’s something mostly irrelevant.   It would be cool if that dot turned to the same color of the calendar or turn into a multi-colored triangle if there are multiple calendar entries for that date. title: Poor App Ratings are Inaccurate
body:
At the time of this review post the ratings for this app are not very good. That’s likely because no one with a good experience thinks to rate a default app that came preinstalled on their phone. I came across it by accident and decided why not leave a review to point this out. 

I’m a very forgetful person. I’ve been using the Calendar app for a year or more. Very organized, useful, and free. Works on iPhone & Mac. If you’re a Windows user like me you may also access your calendar via icloud.com if you use iCloud. 

It’s useful if you wan to set 1-2 alarms or if you want to set 20+ daily alarms like me. I’ve had moments where I have literally 150 alarms going off in a week for reminders, events, etc. As I said- I’m a very forgetful person. 

This app has allowed me to remain relatively organized and keep order in my life despite my forgetfulness. 10/10.

title: Google Month view is better
body:
I love the Apple calendar in so many ways. But the #1 hands down lamest part of Apple calendar: there is no proper list view on iPhone. 

Grab yourself the Google calendar and you’ll see a truly solid month view. Select a month and you can see an overview of the things happening on individual days from above. You can look at month view and quickly see “well, the 16th and 17th im doing these heavy tasks all day so I better not schedule those days. Same with the 23rd.” But not with Apple.

Apple doesn’t make a month view worth your time. Period.

It just shows a stupid dot. Does the dot represent a 20 minute call or an event that will take 8 hours? Does that dot represent “dinner with family” or “breakfast with a client?” Does that dot represent a 14 hour production or a 30 minute meditation course? You don’t know until you click the day. 

So scheduling become a pain on iOS. Imagine many of us who don’t work from a desk- we are out in the world and someone wants to schedule something with us. We pull out our phone and have to tell someone “wait, let me click each day of the week to see which is most convenient because developers at Apple haven’t grasped month view like the people at Google. Sorry. I don’t know what’s wrong with those Apple developers. But it looks like every day of the month is full until I click each day individually!”

Or we can just use Google calendar. Because Apple failed here.

I truly want to use Apple calendar to its fullest but this month view issue is terrible for those of us who actually live/work the mobile life. And, as many zoomers and digital natives hit the work scene, more will switch to google as they need a fast and easy calendar too

title: Add an alarm please!
body:
I have ADHD. I don’t use the calendar for day to day stuff, my life’s not that complicated, but I have scheduled reminders for things my brain will otherwise never remember like bill due dates and my moms birthday. Since the alerts are easy to miss or dismiss, if an event is within one week I use the clock to set an alarm for that day of the week, but it can only be a day of the week, not set for a specific date. I have a ton of calendar events reminding me to set an alarm in two months. 

The reminders app is not aggressive enough for the short term, nor good at scheduling long term, so that’s out entirely. 

What would be ideal is if I could combine the alarm and calendar functions—alarms for calendar events. Please force me to notice the event telling me I’m about to miss my mom’s birthday again.

body:

Also experiencing events jumping from calendar to calendar- my default calendar also keeps changing and I keep changing it back. Who knows maybe I’ve been hacked…but I am swapping to another calendar app. 
I have a very very busy schedule and one dropped or moved event can cause a cascade of issues, not to mention loss of income. Especially if I know I am not the one deleting events. Also there’s no way to turn off multiple alerts for basic events- like birthday calendar & contact calendar showing up in duplicate and triplicate on the calendar. Another disappointment is that it’s difficult to view my month or week at a glance and see my general business status. Makes it twice as difficult to balance work and life if you can’t view what’s happening in an overview.

title: Erases configuration EVERY TIME you use it
body:
I chose to use my Outlook.com calendar because it, unlike iCloud’s calendar, lets you set up 2 alerts per event (like one reminder a week in advance of an appointment and another the day of the appointment).  
However, EVERY time you open Calendar, all of your events are gone because you have to deselect the default iCloud calendar and re-select outlook.com as the default calendar. Note that in iOS’s Settings, the default calendar is set to outlook.com just as it is in Calendar, so I don’t understand the logic behind changing these settings on me EVERY! DANG! TIME!

As others have mentioned, after a recent update to Calendar, they removed the option for a second alert/reminder when creating events, so the one major thing this app had going for it is gone, leaving behind the headache of having to reconfigure the app EVERY time you use it.

title: Extremely limited functionality compared to Mac OS calendar.
body:
iPad iOS Calendar alerts are essentially useless.

On my MacBook Pro, no matter what I am doing, or even if I wake it up past the specified alert time, I always get a small banner at the top right of my screen with a reminder, and I have to click on and acknowledge it in some way in order to remove it. 

No such feature exists with the iPad Calendar. And not only that, if I wake my iPad past the preset alert time, I get no post-reminder at all. Not even in the Notification Center. This renders it essentially useless unless you are active on your iPad prior to the alert setting.

It’s mind-boggling that the iPad Calendar has been engineered in such a way.

title: It decided to be intuitive
body:
Once upon a time I was able to choose whether the default display was month, week or day and it would stay that way. I could tap on a day of the month and that day would open. Now when I tap on an empty date in preparation to enter an appointment the empty date doesn’t show up, all the appointments near the empty date fill the display. For whom is this a helpful feature? Why is there no option to turn off this feature? 
In the olden days there was just a dot for every appointment on a date, you’d have to open the date to see the appointments. Annoying but dependable. Now the first appointment shows up in the date and if there are others it says “other”. At a glance it really looks like there is only one appointment on that day. Instead of making “other” bigger give me the option to go back to dots. One dot, one appointment, 8 dots, 8 appointments. 
Just a few versions ago I was able to choose holiday calendars from anywhere I wanted.  Now it’s only USA holidays so I have to hand enter holidays for home. I can probably change my region but then I can only operate those options. When did Apple become so attached to nationalist ideals? It must be about making somethings more expensive in certain areas. 
The app tries to be intuitive by providing what it thinks I want by default, but it’s more like when a child is being helpful and a short task become a long one that requires loads of patience. The difference is I have no love for the app. 
Just fix it.

title: Good App, BUT …
body:
Dear Apple:
Thank you for making iCalendar and including in on all your iPhones, iPads, and computers. I appreciate it. I use the app every day, every night … all the time! I enjoy it and rely on it. The organization is intuitive and easy to use. Thanks for a great foundation. 

It would be helpful to me if there were a diary function not related to events. This would be helpful to note things which happen on a particular day. For me, I’d like to note when an individual died without making a recurrent “event” out of it. If you could add a “sticky note” function to iCalendar, that would help. However, a full on diary would be the most help. 

Again, thanks for a good app. I appreciate it.

title: Falling behind a bit, mostly good
body:
Needs to integrate with Reminders to catch up with Google Calendar & Tasks, Outlook & To-Do, and every popular calendar app on the App Store

Let events be pinched down to 15 minutes, not 30, like on the iPad

Ideas:

Easily toggle multiple calendars on and off either by tagging them or arranging groups

Design a way to view, edit, and easily share your availability over a span of time to anyone with or without iOS

Optional full-screen alerts for when an event starts, like an alarm. Sometimes I need my attention aggressively pulled away from what I’m doing

Count down to events by year/month/week/day/hour/minute with notifications and a dedicated widget, as a way to extend the concept of early alerts

Match what Google is doing with automatic scheduling of repeating events. Machine-learning-based predictive experiences are very in vogue rn. Make em useful

Optionally show weather conditions with animations similar to Weather within each event. Like a visual way to say “it will be raining or very windy during this event”

Optionally show sunrise/sunset times or indicate daylight in some way

Offer a… idk what to call it. A card view? The thing Readdle’s Calendars has. It’s nice

Google Calendar on Android will help schedule or reschedule recurring goals for you. For example if you want to exercise 3 days a week and say you prefer evenings it’ll find the time on your calendar and schedule it. If you have an important appointment that conflicts it’ll adjust. In short it helps you with the day-to-day tedium of juggling a busy calendar. Apple’s app does nothing around this.
